newsitem.title: CANADA: Molson Breweries to take charge on plant closure.
newsitem.headline: Molson Breweries to take charge on plant closure.

text.p: Molson Breweries, Canada's largest brewer, said on Tuesday that it planned to close its Redwood brewing facility in Winnipeg effective August 1.
As result, Molson Breweries said it will take a C$16 million charge against earnings in the fourth quarter of 1997.

"This will be made up of a C$10 million asset write-down and approximately C$6 million in other costs related to the closure," the brewer said in a statement. Molson Breweries is owned 40 percent each by Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd and Toronto-based Molson Cos Ltd, and 20 percent by Philip Morris Cos' Miller Brewing unit.
Molson Breweries said it was closing the Winnipeg facility due to excess capacity in Western Canada, growing global competition and declining beer consumption.

"Despite the best efforts of the union and management, we have not been able to raise sales in Western Canada to a level that would significantly increase the utilization of the Redwood brewery," said Blair Shier, president of Molson Breweries' Western Canada operations.
The brewery employs 91 hourly and salaried employees. Molson said it would work with an employee group to develop severance packages.

Growth in the microbrewery industry, the emergence of a significant unregulated alcohol (U-Brew) segment and declining overall consumption made for challenging times for the industry, Molson Breweries said.
Once production officially stopped, usable equipment would be redeployed to other Molson facilities throughout the country, the brewer said.
